description: The two January food-ration leads report complaints/objections but provide no attendance estimates. Queue size, ration recipients, and number of affected households cannot be substituted for protesters.
required_followup: Seek contemporaneous reporting or organizer/eyewitness documentation that describes attendance in each action; retain both candidates below threshold review until >=50 is supported.

description: The reports concern state-regulated subsidized food, but do not clearly identify who set the local quantity cuts or whether each buyer action made a collective demand to a state policymaker.
required_followup: Review fuller contemporaneous accounts and any official notice identifying the decision-maker; keep the ration-policy versus store-level target distinction explicit.

description: The reports give dates for ration changes and queues, but not full physical start/end times for the buyer actions; quota restoration and the end of scheduled sales are not physical end evidence.
required_followup: Search same-week follow-up for departure/dissolution or further gatherings; leave end_date null unless a physical end is reported.

description: A January 11 Dashoguz shop account and January 16 Sayat district/Lebap queue are separate dated reports in different locations. Similar ration grievances do not establish shared organization or one campaign episode.
required_followup: Search late December and early February for physical continuity and compare organizers/sites; do not merge solely by shared food-supply issue.

description: For the January 16 queue, only one woman's police detention is reported; other response dimensions remain unknown. For the January 11 account, a quota reversal is reported but the responsible state actor is not identified.
required_followup: Seek source accounts identifying the ration decision-maker and event-specific police/official actions; do not infer silence, dispersal, beatings, or weapons.

description: Both event leads are from Chronicles of Turkmenistan. The outlet attributes information to its correspondents but gives no named event-day witness or independent second outlet in these reports.
required_followup: Seek distinct contemporaneous sources; do not count separate articles from one publisher as independent corroboration.

description: Discovery includes Russian and Turkmen query terms plus English. No independent Turkmen-language reviewer has checked translation or vernacular coverage.
required_followup: Continue Turkmen-language/local-region searches; seek later linguistic review if available.

description: The documented first pass queried all five English and all four Russian January weekly windows, plus limited Turkmen-language terms, and covered Ashgabat/provincial food, employment, housing, wages, and diaspora leads. It has not systematically covered every region, sector, local-language variant, or archive; open-web searching does not reproduce LexisNexis, and an early food-queue lead shaped later discovery.
required_followup: If further discovery is undertaken, broaden regional and issue searches and obtain independent Turkmen-language review where available; preserve the open-web/archive limitations and make no absence or exhaustive-coverage claim.

description: Open-web searches and accessible local articles do not reproduce the original LexisNexis newspaper set or systematic archive coverage.
required_followup: Report this method deviation and avoid absence or exhaustive-coverage claims.

description: The latest official MM event-file bytes, current country universe/schema, and supplemental Coding Procedure remain unverified under the project's existing baseline gate.
required_followup: Coordinator must resolve the official baseline/compatibility gate before any official IDs or merges; this unit does not change that gate.

description: CABAR places a Shatlyk bus-stop job-seeker gathering in its January 2021 review; Radio Azatlyk published on 13 January and Fergana on 14 January. Azatlyk's body says its correspondent reported the incident on 12 August without a year, while Fergana does not state the physical date and explicitly attributes the report to Azatlyk. Physical date/month ownership remain unresolved.
required_followup: Find a contemporaneous source that dates the physical gathering or clarifies the August reference; do not infer event onset from article publication dates.

description: Fergana's 14 January report explicitly attributes the Shatlyk account to Radio Azatlyk, and CABAR links both reports. These are not independent confirmations of turnout/date; Azatlyk is the identified reporting origin.
required_followup: Preserve the shared origin and seek a genuinely independent contemporaneous source if available; do not count CABAR or Fergana as independent corroboration.

description: Turkmen.News body review confirms that S036 describes the same 16 January Sayat queue and detention as E002 and explicitly cites Chronicles of Turkmenistan as its reporting source. It is a derivative report, not independent corroboration; no turnout estimate is added.
required_followup: Seek a genuinely independent contemporaneous account of attendance, event character, and the reported detention if available; do not count S036 as an independent confirmation or use queue/service-area size as turnout.

description: S037 is dated 9 January and says an Azatlyk correspondent was in a Bayramali queue on 8 January; it describes police arriving daily to disperse early-morning queues. S038 now adds reported Bayramali queues on 5 and 6 January, but does not establish these were the same people or episode, or that the earlier queues involved police, protest activity, or an explicit state demand. Physical onset/end of E005’s reported queue/police pattern and its protest status remain unresolved.
required_followup: Seek independent evidence or fuller original reporting that links or distinguishes the 5–6 January queues from the 8 January observation and identifies episode boundaries, active participation, an explicit state demand, and written origin; keep E005 pending evidence if these remain unclear.

description: S038’s limited body read reports Mary-region residents queuing at 4 a.m., describes hundreds in dawn queues (not protest turnout), quotes a Bayramali resident about 5 January, and mentions Bayramali queues at 4 a.m. on 6 January. It credits Radio Azatlyk correspondents, as does the Azatlyk reporting chain identified by S037, but does not establish the same individuals or episode, a protest, an explicit demand, or police contact on 5–6 January. The written byline/republication relationship is unknown; do not treat S038 as an independent confirmation, separate event, or protest count.
required_followup: If a later review finds direct evidence linking or distinguishing these queue observations, assess it without inferring continuity from shared city/topic; seek independent confirmation of protest activity, turnout, demand, and written origin.

description: A CentralAsia.org result says residents queue at empty shops, but its page/event date and relation to E005 are not in the captured header. Later boundary continuity remains unresolved.
required_followup: After the full parse/denial gate, verify the article date and any physical link to the Bayramali queues; keep dates null if the body does not establish onset.

description: A limited Turkmen.News body read reports around 80 women at the local administration in Shatlyk, Mary region, on 10 February 2021 over subsidized-food interruptions and bread-ration reductions. This confirms a separate later-boundary gathering, but the article does not link it to E005's January Bayramali queues; same-region food grievances alone do not establish one continuous episode.
required_followup: Keep the 10 February Shatlyk gathering out of January and do not record it as a continuation. If a later cross-month review finds direct evidence linking the sites or organizer/episode, assess it there; do not merge on issue similarity alone.

description: A diaspora-focused TMHelsinki search result says a planned rally in Istanbul did not take place. The captured title gives no publication date, event date, or policy target, and establishes no actual gathering in Turkmenistan.
required_followup: No January domestic protest is inferred from this result. If overseas activity becomes relevant to a separate review, verify the publication/date and intended target from the page body; keep diaspora events distinct from domestic actions.

description: Q20 returned a 9tv food-price protest headline (S027), an IWPR spontaneous-protest headline (S043), and a 24.kg archive headline (S033). The exact 9tv page returned a Cloudflare 403 denial before article content; publication/event date and all body facts remain unknown and no retry was made. S043 is dated 29 August 2012 and S033 30 August 2012; both discuss 2012 wage disputes including the Lebap bridge-workers strike, and their overlapping account origins are not independently established. They are outside January 2021. No Q20 source establishes another January event.
required_followup: Do not retry or seek a mirror for S027. Do not treat the dated 2012 IWPR/24.kg material as a January 2021 event. If any still-unreviewed discovery lead becomes relevant, check it only after a fresh complete all-unit parse and exact publisher/story denial review; determine January scope, attendance, state demand, response attribution, and reporting origin before creating or linking a candidate.

description: CABAR and linked Fergana report a Mary city administration protest on 21 December 2020 by about 50 women; Fergana says the women left after an official promised to relay their complaints. This establishes the reported end of that gathering, but neither source links it to E005 or any January queue and neither rules out separate later actions. Broader episode linkage remains unknown.
required_followup: Do not record the December gathering as a continuation of E005 and do not infer that no later action occurred. Keep the relationship between the December gathering and January Bayramali queues unresolved unless direct evidence of shared organization or physical continuity emerges.
